name: process-scroll
purpose: The stages of a process as a row of numbered dark cards on a pixel texture, under a section title. On narrow screens the row scrolls sideways with snap; from the large breakpoint up the cards share the width, or, with `pinned`, keep a 26rem card width while the band pins under the site header and the page scroll slides the row sideways until its last card is in view (azion.com's careers hiring process). From the design sample's site `ProcessScroll`.
useWhen: How something works in three to five ordered stages (build, deploy, observe).
avoidWhen: For more than five stages or stages with art — use `FeatureScroll`.
For five to eight short points with no section-title layout — use `StickyCarousel`; for ordered stages that pin while the page scrolls, set `pinned` here.
related: StickyCarousel` — the same cards, always pinned, under a plain section title.
bestPractices: Name each stage with a verb.

Set `pinned` when the stages run wider than the page column (five tall cards, as the careers hiring process): the band stays on screen while the page scroll walks the row. Do not nest a pinned band in a container that clips overflow; sticky positioning needs the page scroll.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a hash link can target it.

props.name: titleKind
props.doc: Alignment of the section title over the card row.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered as its `h2`; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: descriptionWidth
props.doc: Column span of the paragraph: `wide` runs it across the middle column too.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The stages, in order; each is `{ title, description }` and gets its own numbered card.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the scrollable card row; defaults to the title.

props.name: pinned
props.doc: From the large breakpoint, pins the band under the site header while the page scrolls and slides the card row sideways until its last card is in view; below it, or under reduced motion, the row scrolls sideways on its own.

props.name: headerOffset
props.doc: Height of the sticky site header a pinned band sticks under; defaults to the SiteNav bar's token, any CSS length.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'

  const steps = [
    { title: 'Push', description: 'Every push to the main branch builds a new version.' },
    { title: 'Build', description: 'The build runs in an isolated worker with your settings.' },
    {
      title: 'Deploy',
      description: 'The version goes live everywhere at once, with no regions to pick.'
    },
    { title: 'Observe', description: 'Metrics and logs for the new version arrive in seconds.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ProcessScroll
    eyebrow="How it works"
    title="From commit to production"
    description="Four stages, all automatic once the repository is connected."
    :steps="steps"
  />
</template>

examples.name: Pinned
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ProcessScroll from '@aziontech/webkit/process-scroll'

  const steps = [
    { title: 'Role request', description: 'A hiring manager requests a new role.' },
    {
      title: 'Scope and posting',
      description: 'People and the hiring manager scope the role and publish the opening.'
    },
    {
      title: 'Recruiting and interviews',
      description: 'Candidates meet the team in technical and culture interviews.'
    },
    { title: 'Calibration', description: 'The panel compares notes and decides together.' },
    { title: 'Offer letter', description: 'The chosen candidate receives the offer.' }
  ]
</script>

<template>
  <ProcessScroll
    pinned
    title-kind="centered"
    title="Hiring process"
    description="Every role goes through the same five stages, from the first request to the offer."
    :steps="steps"
  />
</template>
